title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan families for every degree
formal: For every fixed integer \(d\ge 3\), is there one deterministic algorithm that computes the port rotation map of connected d-regular Ramanujan graphs for an unbounded set of vertex counts n in time polynomial in log n, with the effective family and graph conventions below?
definitions: The graphs are undirected multigraphs on \([n]=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\); parallel edges and loops are permitted, as in the source’s graph convention. Each vertex has ports \([d]\). A rotation map \(Rot_{n}:[n]\times [d]\to [n]\times [d]\) is an involution: if \(Rot_{n}(v,i)=(w,j)\), then \(Rot_{n}(w,j)=(v,i)\). Paired ports encode an undirected edge; a fixed port encodes a loop. Define the symmetric integer adjacency matrix A by \(A_{vw}=|\){i:the first coordinate of \(Rot_{n}(v,i)\) is w}|, so every row sum is d and a fixed-port loop contributes one to the diagonal and degree. Connectivity means the underlying undirected graph is connected. List the real eigenvalues with multiplicity in decreasing order \(d=\lambda _{1}\ge \cdots \ge \lambda _{n}\). Require |\(\lambda _{i}|\le 2\sqrt{d- 1}\) for \(i\ge 2\), except that the single eigenvalue −d is permitted when the graph is bipartite. For each fixed d the answer supplies a decidable infinite set \(N_{d}\) of positive integers, a single total deterministic bit algorithm \(R_{d}\), and constants \(C_{d},a_{d}\). On input \((n,v,i)\) in binary, \(R_{d}\) runs in at most \(C_{d}(1+\log _{2} n)^{a}_{d}\) steps for valid \(v\in [n],i\in [d]\). For every \(n\in N_{d}\) its outputs constitute the rotation map of such a graph. No graph-dependent advice, preprocessing or tables are supplied to \(R_{d}\); its fixed program may depend on d. The family’s size-membership decider must halt on all binary n but has no prescribed running-time bound. No bound on gaps between successive \(n\in N_{d}\) is required. Outputs at n outside \(N_{d}\) carry no graph promise. This retains the imported infinite-family target, which is weaker than requiring every admissible size; it does not impose simple-graph or non-bipartite restrictions.

context_blocks.text: Ramanujan graphs achieve the optimal asymptotic spectral expansion bound for a fixed degree. Strong explicitness makes their local connectivity available with work polynomial in the vertex-label length.

Explicit and strongly explicit almost-Ramanujan constructions are different from attaining the exact bound at every fixed degree. Alon’s paper carefully separates these guarantees. The personal list’s 2026 signing-preprint citation has been replaced: that preprint was withdrawn and did not support the construction target.

why: Combine extremal spectral quality with efficient local access for arbitrary constant-degree expanders.
answer_criterion: Supply the family decider and rotation algorithms for every d, and prove uniformity in n, unbounded family sizes, connectivity and the exact Ramanujan bound. Alternatively refute the quantified existence assertion for some d. A positive spectral slack, graph-specific advice or a polynomial-in-n adjacency algorithm is insufficient.
